goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration crashes with NoMethodError on fresh installs because embed_category site setting row doesn't exist when never changed from default, so [0] is nil
Migration also fails at line 15 querying 'uncategorized_category_id' which only exists if it was ever set

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, the fallback path does `execute("SELECT value FROM site_settings WHERE name = 'uncategorized_category_id'")[0]['value'].to_i` when `category_id == 0`. If that SELECT returns zero rows, `[0]` is `nil` and `['value']` will raise, causing the migration to fail. The migration does not guard for the setting row being absent.

embedding controller update action persists nothing, making the PUT a no-op that returns 200 and silently discards input

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::EmbeddingController, `update` simply re-renders the current `@embedding` (an OpenStruct built in `fetch_embedding`) and does not read params or persist anything (`def update; render_serialized(@embedding, ...); end`). Since routes expose `put "customize/embedding" => "embedding#update"`, any PUT payload would be ignored while still returning a successful JSON response. However, the UI added in `embedding.hbs` has no save action wired up (only add/delete hosts via `EmbeddableHostsController`), so this is more an incomplete/placeholder endpoint than a currently-triggered functional break.

adjudication_records.issue_text: expandable_first_post? drops the 'any host configured' gate so truncation expands on topics with no embedding setup

adjudication.rationale: In `app/models/topic.rb`, `expandable_first_post?` was changed from `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? && SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` to `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`. The diff removes the “any host configured” gate entirely and does not replace it with a check like `EmbeddableHost.any?`. Therefore, if `embed_truncate` is enabled and a topic has a `topic_embed`, `expandable_first_post?` will return true even when there are no allowed embeddable hosts configured (i.e., embedding effectively not set up).

adjudication_records.issue_text: store.js pluralize assumes a pluralize method on the store that is never defined, risking TypeError or wrong hydration keys

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = ...` in `store.js` when hydrating `*_ids`, but the finding’s claim that `pluralize` is “never defined” is not verifiable from the diff (the method could exist elsewhere in `store.js` outside the shown hunk or on the store prototype). Additionally, the updated JS tests exercise the new plural hydration (`color_ids` -> `colors`) and would fail if `pluralize` were actually missing, suggesting it exists in the codebase.

adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the migration indexing into execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking for an empty result set, causing a crash on fresh installs when the embed_category row/setting is missing, which can break related functionality.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Same nil-crash pattern in migration at line 17 for uncategorized_category_id lookup

adjudication.rationale: In the new migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the fallback query `execute("SELECT value FROM site_settings WHERE name = 'uncategorized_category_id'")[0]['value'].to_i` assumes the result set has at least one row. If the `site_settings` row is missing (or the query returns no rows for any reason), `[0]` will be `nil` and `['value']` will raise, breaking the migration. There is no nil/empty check around this lookup.

matched_golden_ids: Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

This is the same underlying concern as the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: expandable_first_post? dropped the SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? guard, so topics with embeds remain truncated even when all embeddable hosts are deleted

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/topic.rb, `expandable_first_post?` was changed from `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? && SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` to `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`, removing any check that embedding is currently enabled/allowed. Since `has_topic_embed?` can remain true for previously embedded topics even after all `EmbeddableHost` records are deleted, setting `SiteSetting.embed_truncate` true will still make posts expandable/truncated regardless of current allowed hosts. The new tests don’t cover the case where `embed_truncate` is true and `has_topic_embed?` is true with zero embeddable hosts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Corresponding spec 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' is vacuous — passes only because Fabricate.build(:topic) has no topic embed

adjudication.rationale: In `spec/models/topic_spec.rb` under `describe "expandable_first_post?"`, the example `it "is false if embeddable_host is blank"` has no setup to make `expandable_first_post?` true except for the “blank host” condition: it does not set `SiteSetting.embed_truncate = true` and does not stub `topic.has_topic_embed?` to true (those are only done in the later nested `describe 'with an emeddable host'`). Since the implementation is now `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`, the test will pass because one/both defaults are false, not because embeddable hosts are blank, making the spec effectively vacuous/misleading.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin embeddable_hosts_controller#update with nonexistent id calls save_host(nil) raising NoMethodError, returning 500 instead of 404

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update`, the code does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then unconditionally calls `save_host(host)` (new file `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb`). If no record exists, `host` is `nil`, and `save_host` immediately executes `host.host = ...` / `host.category_id = ...`, which will raise `NoMethodError` and result in a 500 rather than a 404/not-found response.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Controller accesses params[:embeddable_host][:host] without checking param hash, raising 500 instead of 4xx when missing

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host`, the code directly dereferences nested params (`params[:embeddable_host][:host]` and `params[:embeddable_host][:category_id]`) without checking that `params[:embeddable_host]` exists. If the request omits that hash, this will raise `NoMethodError` (`nil[:host]`) and result in a 500 instead of a handled 4xx validation/error response.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin::EmbeddingController#update renders serializer without reading or persisting any params — PUT route, action, and save button are dead code that saves nothing

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` simply `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)` and never reads or persists any params (it also builds `@embedding` from an `OpenStruct` in `fetch_embedding`, so there’s nothing to save). On the client, `admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6` defines a `saveChanges` action that calls `this.get('embedding').update({})`, which would hit the new PUT `/admin/customize/embedding` route, but there is no corresponding server-side update logic. However, the provided template (`admin/templates/embedding.hbs`) doesn’t include a save button or call `saveChanges`, and host CRUD is handled via `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController`, so this is more “dead/placeholder endpoint + unused action” than a user-visible broken behavior shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fabricator files have swapped contents: category_fabricator.rb defines :embeddable_host and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb holds the category fabricators
matched_golden_ids: The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate explicitly states that the contents of category_fabricator.rb and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb are swapped (category_fabricator defines :embeddable_host and the other contains category fabricators), which is the same underlying issue described in the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No JS tests for the new admin embedding UI (route, controller, component with buffered save/rollback logic), leaving refactor-sensitive behavior unverified

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new admin embedding UI surface (new Ember route `admin-embedding.js.es6`, controller `admin-embedding.js.es6`, adapter `admin/adapters/embedding.js.es6`, and component `admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6` with buffered save/rollback + delete confirmation, plus new templates). However, there are no corresponding JS/acceptance/component tests added under `test/javascripts/**` to exercise this new route/controller/component behavior; the only JS tests modified are unrelated store hydration tests (`test/javascripts/models/store-test.js.es6` and pretender fixtures). This leaves the new UI logic unverified and refactor-sensitive.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No spec exercises the migration's data path

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a nontrivial data migration (db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb) that reads existing site_settings (embeddable_hosts, embed_category), inserts rows into embeddable_hosts, and deletes the old settings. The added specs cover controllers/models, but there is no spec in the diff that executes or validates this migration’s data-migration behavior (e.g., that settings are correctly converted and then removed).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin embeddable_hosts_controller specs only assert subclass ancestry — no request-level specs cover create/update/destroy

adjudication.rationale: The new spec `spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb` only contains a single example asserting `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController < Admin::AdminController` and does not exercise any of the newly added request actions (`create`, `update`, `destroy`) or the nontrivial parameter-handling logic in `save_host` (e.g., `params[:embeddable_host][:host]`, `category_id` defaulting to `uncategorized_category_id`). This is a concrete, diff-grounded test coverage gap for new behavior, not an immediate functional defect shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: admin/embedding_controller.rb update endpoint is a no-op that saves nothing and doesn't accept params, while UI saveChanges PUTs to it — dead code / unfinished work

adjudication.rationale: Diff shows `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` simply re-renders `@embedding` without applying params or persisting anything (`app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`), while the Ember controller defines `saveChanges()` calling `this.get('embedding').update({});` (`admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6`) and routes/adapters wire a PUT to `/admin/customize/embedding`. However, the template `admin/templates/embedding.hbs` has no UI element invoking `saveChanges`, and actual persistence of hosts is handled via `EmbeddableHost` create/update/destroy. So this is verifiable as dead/no-op plumbing or unfinished work, but not clearly a user-facing defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test fabricator files were swapped: embeddable_host_fabricator.rb now defines base category fabricator and category_fabricator.rb defines embeddable_host, misleading file naming

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` was changed to define `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` (and no longer defines the category-related fabricators), while the newly added `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` now contains the `Fabricator(:category)` and other category variants. This is misleading file naming/organization that could confuse future maintainers and make it harder to locate/modify fabricators, even if the test suite still loads all fabricator files.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unrelated test cleanup in topic_spec.rb for_digest tests (dropping unused topic locals) is diff noise not traceable to the feature

adjudication.rationale: In spec/models/topic_spec.rb, the PR changes two for_digest tests by removing unused local assignments (e.g., `topic = Fabricate(...)` -> just `Fabricate(...)`) without affecting assertions. This is unrelated to the embedding feature and is verifiable diff noise rather than a functional change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Core store.js.es6 hydration extended with plural *_ids support also silently changes basePath semantics for every model via type.replace('_', '-'), a global behavior change better handled by a feature-local adapter

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce a global behavior change in `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/adapters/rest.js.es6`: `basePath(store, type)` now checks `ADMIN_MODELS.indexOf(type.replace('_', '-'))`, which alters how *all* model type strings are interpreted for admin-path routing (even though it only affects whether they match `ADMIN_MODELS`). This could reasonably be raised as a scope/architecture concern (arguably better solved via a dedicated adapter for the new admin model) rather than a verifiable functional bug. The `_hydrateEmbedded` plural `*_ids` support is also a core/global store change, but the finding’s main claim about global basePath semantics is grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration uses raw SQL deletes inside change making it irreversible and destructive: rollback loses embeddable_hosts and embed_category site settings permanently

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, the migration is defined with `def change` but includes destructive raw SQL (`execute "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')"`). This is not reversible (Rails cannot infer how to restore deleted settings), and rollback would not recreate the removed `site_settings` rows, causing permanent loss of those configuration values.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration under-scoped error handling: if embed_category JOIN and uncategorized lookup both fail, category_id is 0 and inserted host rows violate null:false/FK constraints

adjudication.rationale: In the migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts`, `category_id` is defined as `null: false`, but inserting `0` would not violate a NOT NULL constraint (0 is non-null), and the migration does not add any foreign key constraint on `category_id` that would fail for 0. Also, if the `SELECT ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'` returns no rows, `execute(...)[0]` would be `nil` and `['id']` would raise before any inserts, rather than silently producing `category_id = 0` and then inserting rows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: expandable_first_post? lost its 'hosts configured' guard (SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? removed), changing embed-truncation behavior for existing installs with empty embeddable_hosts table

adjudication.rationale: In `app/models/topic.rb`, `expandable_first_post?` changes from `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? && SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` to `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`, removing the “hosts configured” gate entirely. With the new DB-backed allowlist (`EmbeddableHost`), there is no replacement check for `EmbeddableHost.any?`/presence, so on an install where the migrated `embeddable_hosts` table is empty, embedded topics can now return true for `expandable_first_post?` as long as `embed_truncate` is enabled and the topic has an embed, which is a verifiable behavior change introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration crashes with NoMethodError on fresh installs because SELECT for 'embed_category' setting returns nil and nil['id'] raises, blocking db:migrate; no guard for absent row unlike the guarded query below

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration does `execute("SELECT ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i`. If that SELECT returns zero rows (likely on fresh installs where `site_settings` has no row for embed_category), `[0]` is nil and `nil['id']` will raise NoMethodError before the later `if category_id == 0` fallback can run. This matches the finding and would block `db:migrate`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Port is accepted at write time (validation regex allows :port, before_validation only strips scheme/path) but lookup uses uri.host which strips the port, so saved hosts with ports are permanently rejected by host_allowed?

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbeddableHost`, the validation regex allows an optional port (`(:[0-9]{1,5})?`) and `before_validation` strips only scheme and path, leaving ports intact (e.g. `example.com:3000`). But `record_for_host` parses the incoming URL and compares `uri.host` (which excludes the port) against the stored `host` column via `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`. As a result, a saved host with a port will never match and `host_allowed?` will reject it permanently.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No UNIQUE constraint on embeddable_hosts.host; duplicates and case variants both validate and collide on lower(host) lookup, so duplicate row's category is silently ignored

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `embeddable_hosts` without any DB-level unique index/constraint on `host` (migration `create_table :embeddable_hosts` adds only `host`/`category_id`). The model also lacks a `validates_uniqueness_of` and does not normalize case (only strips scheme/path). Lookup uses `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first`, so case variants (and other duplicates) can exist and the “first” row wins, potentially selecting the wrong `category_id` in `TopicEmbed.import` (`eh.try(:category_id)`) and silently ignoring the other duplicate(s).

adjudication_records.issue_text: where("lower(host) = ?") is non-sargable with no index on host, causing O(n) sequential scan on hot path of every embed request; a unique functional index on lower(host) would fix this

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` which queries `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` (app/models/embeddable_host.rb). The migration creating `embeddable_hosts` adds no index on `host` nor a functional index on `lower(host)` (db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb). Since `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` is now called on embed request paths (`EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`), this can become a performance issue due to sequential scans; adding a functional/unique index on `lower(host)` would address it. This is a real, diff-grounded performance concern, not a correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PUT /admin/customize/embedding update endpoint is a no-op that reports success — never writes data, only re-fetches and re-serializes; client saveChanges sends update that can never change anything

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the PUT endpoint is effectively a no-op: `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` just `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)` and `@embedding` is rebuilt in `fetch_embedding` from `EmbeddableHost.all` (no params applied, no persistence). On the client, `admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6#saveChanges` calls `this.get('embedding').update({})`, which cannot change anything server-side. However, the `embedding.hbs` template added in this diff doesn’t invoke `saveChanges` (no save button), and actual host edits persist via the separate `EmbeddableHost` resource (`host.save(props)`), so this is more an unused/misleading API/UI hook than a clearly user-facing defect in the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: record_for_host returns false as a not-found/malformed sentinel alongside nil-or-record, conflating URL malformed with host not allowed and forcing defensive try calls

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/embeddable_host.rb, record_for_host returns `false` for malformed/blank URIs (`return false unless uri.present?` / `return false unless host.present?`) but returns an AR record or `nil` for “not found” (`where(...).first`). This mixes sentinel values (false vs nil) and conflates “malformed URL” with “no matching allowed host” unless callers add special handling. The diff shows callers using `.present?` (host_allowed?) and `.try` (TopicEmbed.import), so it doesn’t manifest as a concrete defect here, but it is a real, diff-grounded API/clarity concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embeddable_hosts.category_id has no foreign key and no index; deleting a category leaves orphan rows that still resolve, causing embeds to land in a dangling category_id passed to PostCreator

adjudication.rationale: The migration creates `embeddable_hosts` with `category_id` (null: false) but adds no index or foreign key constraint (db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb). Nothing in the diff establishes dependent cleanup if a Category is deleted, so `embeddable_hosts` rows can become orphaned. The embed import path uses that value directly: `eh = EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)` then `PostCreator.new(... category: eh.try(:category_id), skip_validations: true, ...)` (app/models/topic_embed.rb). With an orphaned `category_id`, embeds can attempt to create topics with a dangling/nonexistent category reference, which is broken behavior and data integrity loss.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Category and embeddable_host fabricator file contents are swapped (accidental file-swap in diff), so category fabricators live in embeddable_host_fabricator.rb and vice versa, risking future developer confusion

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` was changed to define `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` (host + category), while the newly added `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains the `Fabricator(:category)` and related category variants. This is effectively a file-content/name swap. It’s not necessarily a runtime defect if the test suite loads all fabricators regardless of filename, but it is a concrete, diff-grounded maintainability issue that can confuse future developers and make fabricator lookup harder.

adjudication_records.issue_text: admin/embedding_controller.rb update endpoint is a silent no-op: never reads params, never saves, returns success while discarding admin changes

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` simply re-renders `@embedding` and never reads `params` or persists anything (it’s a no-op PUT endpoint). However, the actual admin “changes” in this PR (adding/editing/deleting allowed hosts) are saved via `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` (`host.save(props)` / `destroyRecord()`), and the `embedding.hbs` template doesn’t expose a “saveChanges” action/button. So the endpoint being a no-op is verifiable, but the claim that it “discards admin changes” isn’t supported by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: fetch_embedding re-reads hosts from DB on every request so the response shows old hosts and UI changes never round-trip; the singleton embedding model has no mutable attributes so the update route exists only for REST shape

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `Admin::EmbeddingController#fetch_embedding` always builds the embedding response from `EmbeddableHost.all.order(:host)` (current DB state), so it would reflect newly created/updated/deleted hosts, not “old hosts” (app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb). UI changes *do* round-trip via the `embeddable-host` model hitting `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` (`create/update/destroy` persist to DB), independent of the embedding singleton (`host.save(...)`, `destroyRecord()` in the component). While `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` doesn’t mutate anything and appears to exist mainly for REST shape, that does not imply the UI changes don’t persist.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic.rb expandable_first_post? silently drops the embeddable_hosts.present? guard, changing behavior so it returns true for any embedded topic even when no hosts are configured

adjudication.rationale: In Topic#expandable_first_post? the condition `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? && ...` was changed to `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` (app/models/topic.rb), with no replacement check for whether any EmbeddableHost records exist. This means if `embed_truncate` is enabled and `has_topic_embed?` is true, the method can now return true even when no hosts are configured (e.g., all EmbeddableHost rows removed). The updated spec still describes behavior in terms of “embeddable host” presence but the method no longer enforces that, indicating an unintended semantic drop.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed_controller.rb collapses the distinct 'embeddable hosts not set' error into the generic 'invalid referer host' error, losing diagnostic distinction

adjudication.rationale: Verified in app/controllers/embed_controller.rb: the prior separate check `raise ... 'embeddable hosts not set' if SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.blank?` was removed, and the only remaining failure is `raise ... 'invalid referer host' unless EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer)`. This does collapse the distinct “no hosts configured” diagnostic into the generic invalid-host error. Behavior still denies embedding when no hosts exist, but the error messaging/diagnostic distinction is lost rather than introducing a functional correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: category_fabricator.rb contents were silently replaced by the embeddable_host fabricator while category fabricators were moved to embeddable_host_fabricator.rb, misleading file organization and git history

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` was rewritten to define `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` instead of category-related fabricators, while a new file `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains the previous `:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, and `:private_category` fabricators. This supports the finding that the fabricator definitions were effectively swapped/moved in a way that can mislead file organization and complicate git history/blame, though it does not directly introduce broken runtime behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration unconditionally destroys old embeddable_hosts/embed_category settings even though the backfill is non-atomic, uses name-based category matching with silent fallback, causing potential data loss with no recovery

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` ends by unconditionally deleting the legacy settings via `execute "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')"`. However, its backfill can silently produce the wrong `category_id`: it derives `category_id` by joining `site_settings.value` to `categories.name` (name-based match) and falls back to `uncategorized_category_id` when no match is found (`if category_id == 0 ...`). That means an existing `embed_category` value that doesn’t exactly match a category name will be lost and replaced with uncategorized, with no way to recover the original setting after the delete. This is diff-grounded potential data/config loss.

adjudication_records.issue_text: SQL injection in migration via string-interpolated embeddable_hosts site-setting value in raw INSERT

adjudication.rationale: The migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` builds raw SQL with string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`, where `h` comes from the persisted `site_settings` value for `embeddable_hosts` (admin-configurable). Because `h` is not quoted/escaped via bound parameters, a value containing `'` or SQL fragments could break the statement or execute unintended SQL during migration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Port-normalization mismatch: stored hosts may include ports but record_for_host compares against uri.host which excludes the port, silently ignoring port restrictions

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbeddableHost`, the validation regex explicitly allows an optional port (`(:[0-9]{1,5})?`), and the `before_validation` normalization strips protocol and path but does not strip or normalize ports (so a value like `example.com:3000` can be stored). However `record_for_host` parses the incoming URL with `URI(host)` and compares `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)`, and `uri.host` excludes the port. This causes a mismatch: entries stored with ports will never match, and conversely entries stored without ports implicitly allow any port. That’s a real behavioral defect visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: params[:id] nil-crash (NoMethodError 500) in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update/destroy when record is missing

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update` and `#destroy`, the record is fetched via `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then used without a nil check. If no record matches (e.g., missing/invalid `params[:id]`), `update` calls `save_host(host)` where `host` is nil and immediately dereferenced (`host.host = ...`), and `destroy` calls `host.destroy` on nil—both causing a `NoMethodError` 500.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Referer used as authorization signal for X-Frame/ensure_embeddable check is client-spoofable

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, access is gated by `request.referer` (now via `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer)`), which is derived from the HTTP Referer header and can be supplied/spoofed by non-browser clients. Since this referer check is used as an authorization/allowlist mechanism for embedding, relying on a client-controlled header is a security weakness that is directly present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin::EmbeddingController#update is a no-op: re-serializes freshly-built OpenStruct and persists nothing, so embedding settings never save

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`, `update` does not read any params or persist anything; it simply re-serializes `@embedding`, which is rebuilt each request in `fetch_embedding` as an `OpenStruct` (`id: 'default', embeddable_hosts: EmbeddableHost.all...`). So the finding that `#update` is a no-op is verifiably true. However, the diff also adds full CRUD for saving hosts via `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` and the Ember UI saves via `host.save(...)` / `destroyRecord()` rather than calling `EmbeddingController#update` (the `embedding.hbs` template has no save button wired to `saveChanges`). Thus, “embedding settings never save” is not directly shown as broken behavior in this PR; it’s more an incomplete/unused endpoint or future feature gap than a demonstrated defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin::EmbeddableHostsController spec only asserts class inheritance with zero request tests for create/update/destroy, so the new controller behavior is untested

adjudication.rationale: In spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb the only example asserts `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController < Admin::AdminController` and does not exercise any of the newly added controller actions in app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb (create/update/destroy) or their parameter handling and responses. Given the controller contains nontrivial behavior (e.g., `save_host` assigns `host`/`category_id`, defaults to `uncategorized_category_id`, and renders serialized JSON or errors), the lack of request/action coverage is a concrete, diff-grounded testing gap.

adjudication_records.issue_text: update and destroy actions do EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first with no nil check, causing NoMethodError/500 on nonexistent host id
matched_golden_ids: The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue points out that update/destroy fetch the record with `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` without checking for nil, leading to NoMethodError/500 when the ID does not exist. This is the same underlying problem described in the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin::EmbeddingController spec only asserts subclass lineage; the EmbeddingSerializer contract (embeddable_host_ids via embed: :ids) is asserted nowhere

adjudication.rationale: The added specs for Admin::EmbeddingController (and Admin::EmbeddableHostsController) only assert inheritance (spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb). Meanwhile, the new serialization/hydration behavior depends on EmbeddingSerializer declaring `has_many :embeddable_hosts, ... embed: :ids` (app/serializers/embedding_serializer.rb), which implies an `embeddable_host_ids` contract that is now supported by the store hydration change for `/_id(s?)$/` (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6). There is no server-side spec asserting the EmbeddingController/EmbeddingSerializer response structure includes the expected `embeddable_host_ids` (or correct sideload), so the finding about an untested serializer contract is accurate and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: JS store test verifies hydration from pretender's hand-written fixtures, not from the Rails serializer output, so the two ends of the serializer contract are each tested against their own fiction

adjudication.rationale: The updated JS store hydration tests (`test/javascripts/models/store-test.js.es6`) exercise `_hydrateEmbedded` using Pretender’s hand-authored JSON fixtures (`test/javascripts/helpers/create-pretender.js.es6` with `__rest_serializer`, `fruit`, `farmers`, `colors`, `color_ids`). Nothing in the diff connects these tests to actual Rails serializer/controller output (e.g., `EmbeddingSerializer`, `EmbeddableHostSerializer`), so the client-side “serializer contract” is being validated against mocked payloads rather than server-generated JSON. That’s a real testing gap/architecture concern but not a runtime defect shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_spec test 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' now passes for the wrong reason since the SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? guard was removed from Topic#expandable_first_post?, leaving the semantic change unverified

adjudication.rationale: In `Topic#expandable_first_post?` the guard `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?` was removed (`SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` only). In `spec/models/topic_spec.rb`, the test `it "is false if embeddable_host is blank"` no longer sets any state that would make the method true (it doesn’t set `SiteSetting.embed_truncate = true` or stub `has_topic_embed?`), so it will return false due to default settings / `has_topic_embed?` being false, not because embeddable hosts are blank. This means the spec no longer verifies the previous “no embeddable hosts => false” behavior (or any new equivalent check, e.g. `EmbeddableHost` presence), making the semantic change untested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Category fabricator file contents were swapped: category_fabricator.rb now defines the :embeddable_host fabricator and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb defines the :category fabricators, creating a change-safety hazard

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` was changed to define `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` (and no longer defines category fabricators), while `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` now contains the `Fabricator(:category)` / `:diff_category` / etc. definitions. This file/name mismatch is confusing and brittle (future changes or selective requires could easily break), but it’s not necessarily a runtime defect if the test helper loads all fabricator files via a glob.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embeddable_host specs only cover the happy path; validation failure branch and record_for_host early-false paths (malformed URI, URI without host) have no tests

adjudication.rationale: In the new `spec/models/embeddable_host_spec.rb`, tests cover trimming (`before_validation`) and the positive/negative cases of `host_allowed?` for normal URLs/domains, but there are no tests for `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host`'s early-return paths (`uri = URI(host) rescue nil; return false unless uri.present?` and `return false unless uri.host.present?`) such as a malformed URI or a URI without a host. Also, while `EmbeddableHost` has `validates_format_of :host`, the specs do not exercise an invalid host that would hit the validation failure path (and therefore the controller `render_json_error(host)` branch in `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host`). This is a specific, diff-grounded test coverage gap rather than a demonstrated defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The nil-embed-host case in topic_embed.rb (feed URL from host not in table → category: nil → PostCreator without category) is exercised by no test

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new logic in `app/models/topic_embed.rb` to derive the category from the embeddable host record: `eh = EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)` and `category: eh.try(:category_id)`. The updated spec `spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb` only covers the happy path by fabricating an `embeddable_host` and asserting `post.topic.category == embeddable_host.category`; it does not exercise the case where `record_for_host(url)` returns nil (host not in table), which would pass `category: nil` to `PostCreator`. This is a specific missing test for newly added nontrivial behavior, but the diff alone doesn’t prove this leads to a runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration crashes with NoMethodError when embed_category site setting is unset or matches no category, because execute(...)[0]['id'] indexes into an empty result set, blocking deploys on default-configured instances

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration does `execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i` on the result of a JOIN against `site_settings` for `embed_category`. If that query returns zero rows (e.g., the setting is unset/blank, missing, or doesn’t match any category name), `execute(...)[0]` will be nil and `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError, so the later `if category_id == 0` fallback never runs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Insert is guarded by embeddable_hosts.cmd_tuples > 0 which is always 0 for a SELECT in PostgreSQL, so the INSERT never executes while the unconditional DELETE FROM site_settings runs, destroying existing embeddable-hosts configuration with zero rows migrated

adjudication.rationale: In the migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the SELECT result is gated by `embeddable_hosts && embeddable_hosts.cmd_tuples > 0`. With PostgreSQL `execute(...)` returns a `PG::Result`, and `cmd_tuples` is not a reliable way to detect returned rows for a `SELECT` (it commonly yields 0/empty for SELECTs), so the block that reads `val` and performs the INSERTs can be skipped even when the row exists. The migration then unconditionally runs `execute "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')"`, which would drop the old configuration without migrating it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Host values are string-interpolated into raw SQL with no escaping and no normalization (no http:// prefix strip, path strip, or downcasing), causing stored hosts with scheme/path/uppercase to never match record_for_host's lower(host) = uri.host comparison, and single quotes abort the migration
matched_golden_ids: record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The golden issue is about a case-insensitive SQL comparison using lower(host) while not downcasing the input parameter, leading to mixed-case hosts not matching. The candidate explicitly calls out lack of normalization/downcasing causing uppercase hosts to not match the lower(host) comparison. Although it adds extra concerns (SQL interpolation/escaping, scheme/path stripping), it still identifies the same underlying case-normalization bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: DELETE FROM site_settings inside def change is irreversible with no backup/export step: rollback reverses create_table but cannot restore deleted setting rows, leaving no path to recover original configuration

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration is written with `def change` but performs raw SQL `execute "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')"`. Rails cannot automatically reverse that deletion on rollback (and there is no `reversible`/`down` logic to re-insert prior values), so rolling back would drop the new table and also leave the old site_settings rows permanently removed. This is a real, diff-grounded concern about migration irreversibility / rollback safety.

adjudication_records.issue_text: create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true drops an existing table and all its data if the migration is re-applied against a partially-migrated or re-baselined database; a new table needs no force

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration uses `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true`. `force: true` will drop and recreate the table if it already exists, which can cause data loss in atypical but real scenarios (e.g., rerunning the migration in a partially-migrated DB or where the table was pre-created). In normal Rails migration flow this file runs once on a fresh DB where the table doesn’t exist, so it’s not a guaranteed defect introduced by the diff, but it is a concrete, diff-grounded risk and unnecessary for a new table.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed_category fallback chain resolves category by name join (s.value = c.name), which mis-resolves when a category was renamed, and the == 0 sentinel conflates 'not found' with an absent setting; lookup should be a safe single query with nil handling

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration derives category_id via `execute("SELECT c.id ... INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i`. This is brittle: (1) if the `embed_category` setting row is missing or its value no longer matches `categories.name` (e.g., category renamed), the query can return 0 rows and `[0]` will be nil, causing the migration to raise before reaching the `category_id == 0` fallback; (2) even when it doesn’t crash, tying to `c.name` can mis-map after renames. The finding’s concern about unsafe lookup / nil handling is grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: update in embeddable_hosts_controller.rb: nil host from where(id:).first causes NoMethodError and 500 instead of 404/422

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update`, the code does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then unconditionally calls `save_host(host)`. If no record matches, `host` is `nil` and `save_host` immediately does `host.host = ...`, causing a `NoMethodError` and a 500 instead of a proper 404/422 response. The same nil dereference risk exists in `#destroy` where `host.destroy` is called without checking for `nil`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: destroy in embeddable_hosts_controller.rb: nil host causes NoMethodError 500 when deleting nonexistent/already-deleted host

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#destroy`, the code does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` followed by `host.destroy` without a nil check. If the record doesn’t exist (nonexistent/already deleted id), `host` will be `nil` and `nil.destroy` will raise `NoMethodError`, resulting in a 500.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embedding_controller.rb update never reads params or persists anything but returns 200, causing silent no-op saves (P0)

adjudication.rationale: In the new `Admin::EmbeddingController` (`app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`), `update` does not read `params` or persist anything; it simply re-renders the serialized `@embedding`. The client-side controller also defines a `saveChanges` action that calls `this.get('embedding').update({});` which would hit that PUT endpoint and get a 200 with no state change. However, the provided `embedding.hbs` template does not invoke `saveChanges` (it only adds/deletes/saves hosts via the `embeddable-host` component and `embeddable_hosts` REST resource), so this looks like an unused/incomplete endpoint/action rather than a demonstrated broken flow in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embeddable-host.js.es6 delete lacks .catch on destroyRecord, so failures surface no error and the row remains

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6`, the `delete()` action calls `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(() => { this.sendAction('deleteHost', this.get('host')); });` with no `.catch(...)`. If the DELETE request fails, the promise rejection is unhandled and no error is surfaced (unlike `save()`, which uses `.catch(popupAjaxError)`), leaving the UI in a confusing state with no feedback.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embeddable-host.js.es6 save uses findById(null) which returns undefined, desyncing displayed category from persisted state with no rollback

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6` the `save()` action sets `props.category_id = this.get('categoryId')`. For a newly added host (`addHost()` creates a record with no category and `categoryId` defaults to `null`), the server normalizes blank `category_id` to `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id` (`Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host`). However, the client then does `host.set('category', Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId')));` inside the save success handler. If `categoryId` is `null`, `findById(null)` yields `undefined`, and the UI will show no category (`{{category-badge host.category}}`) despite the persisted state being uncategorized. No rollback/fixup occurs, so this is a real correctness bug introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: store.js.es6 plural-ID hydration writes [null] entries when referenced ids missing from payload, causing null deref in templates

adjudication.rationale: In `store.js.es6` `_hydrateEmbedded`, the new plural-ID branch (`/(.+)\_id(s?)$/` with `m[2]`) does `obj[k].map(id => self._lookupSubType(...))` and assigns the array directly to `obj[self.pluralize(subType)]`. If `_lookupSubType` returns `null`/`undefined` for an id not present in the embedded payload, the resulting array will contain `null` entries (no filtering/compaction is done). The finding’s downstream “null deref in templates” is plausible but not directly shown in this diff; the unfiltered-null hydration behavior itself is diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddableHost.all loaded with no limit and host_allowed? does an uncached per-request DB query on the hot embed path

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces DB-backed embeddable host checks. `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` now calls `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer)` (and `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` does the same), which performs `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` in `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host`, i.e., a DB query per request with no caching shown. Separately, the admin embedding payload loads `EmbeddableHost.all.order(:host)` in `Admin::EmbeddingController#fetch_embedding`, which is an unbounded load. These are performance/scalability concerns grounded in the diff, not a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embeddable_host.rb before_validation mutates self.host in-place with sub!, leaving mutated value on validation failure so error messages show trimmed host

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/embeddable_host.rb, the `before_validation` callback uses `self.host.sub!(...)` twice, which mutates the `host` attribute in-place before validations run. If the subsequent `validates_format_of :host` fails, the model will still have the trimmed host value, so any validation errors (and UI displaying the invalid value) would reflect the mutated/normalized input rather than what the user originally entered. This is a real, diff-grounded behavior concern, but it’s not clearly a correctness defect in functionality.
